thread.title: Apple's Self-Driving Tech Project May Be Closer Than It Appears - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Roman Luzgin
title: Apple's Self-Driving Tech Project May Be Closer Than It Appears - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Apple as an automotive company Although Apple ( AAPL ) is still considered to be an "iPhone company" by many investors, it is not a secret the corporation is actively pursuing projects in other important areas. Many of those projects, like Apple Music and other services, are already paying off, evident by $9.2 billion in revenue generated by the services segment in the latest quarter. Recently, the company has entered the field of healthcare, which can potentially become one of the biggest addressable markets for the company. However, one of the most mysterious yet promising projects remains to be an anticipated "Apple Car."
The car itself is not likely to appear as a product in Apple's portfolio, but it is becoming more evident that the automotive technology is something the company will reveal at some point in the future. To remind, a year ago Apple CEO Tim Cook admitted working on autonomous systems for cars, which include such technology as self driving. Recent developments in this area show that this future may be closer than it can seem.
Cook did not explicitly lay out Apple’s plans, but he spoke of “three vectors of change” that are set to disrupt the auto industry - self-driving cars, electric cars, and ride-sharing companies - and he did say that his company is focusing on “autonomous systems.”
Why is this important for investors? The main reason is the significant potential of the market, which means Apple will have a big room to grow in case it enters the automotive space. Hence, several studies estimate that technology will enable "new global Passenger Economy worth $7 trillion annually in 2050," which means that a corporation able to capture at least 0.1% of the market will enjoy $7,000,000,000 in additional revenue. Notably, digital demand is listed as one of the main challenges for the players in the auto market, which, again, means there's an opportunity for Apple to meet this demand.
Apple and self-driving technology While Tim Cook has not spoken publicly about Apple's automotive efforts since the aforementioned interview that he gave in June last year, there has been some news that can shed light on the current status of the project and its possible future.
First of all, it seems that Apple takes self-driving tech seriously, as the company continues to increase its fleet of test vehicles. Hence, it was reported earlier in May that the tech giant now has state permission to test 55 cars on public roads of California, compared to just three cars last year. The number looks impressive in light of the fact that such pioneers of autonomous driving tech such as Waymo ( GOOG )( GOOGL ), Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) have fewer vehicles in the Golden State, and the only player with more autonomous driving permissions is General Motors ( GM ). It is stated by TechCrunch:
In order to conduct driverless testing, companies must have previously tested the vehicles in controlled conditions. The vehicles must also, among many other things, meet the definition of an SAE Level 4 or 5 vehicle.
Therefore, Apple having permission to test 55 cars means at least two critical things:
The corporation has already tested self-driving vehicles. This implies Apple has all the necessary equipment (radars, lidars, cameras), vehicles, software, and facilities for in-house tests. Apple achieved at least level 4 automation according to the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) definition. In turn, level 4 states "no human interaction required," which is another clue that shows the level of progress of Apple's self-driving tech. Level 4 vehicles are able to intervene themselves if things go wrong or there is a system failure. In this sense, these cars are left completely to their own devices without any human intervention in the vast majority of situations.
Patents are another source of information when it comes to Apple's self-driving tech. One of the latest filings demonstrated how Apple is going to merge automotive technology with its other area of expertise - augmented reality. AR became one of the crucial improvements in the latest iOS, as Apple paid a lot of attention to this technology during last year's WWDC conference, introducing ARKit for developers.
The description of the patent shows that the main idea of this technology is to use AR for 3-D visualization of things that are out of driver's view, like roads, trees, or hills that are in the distance from a vehicle. One of the images provides an example of what the final solution can look like in real life.
As another example, augmented reality systems may utilize remote sensing devices to provide depth information about objects in an environment. In some scenarios, laser-based sensing technologies, such as light ranging and detection (LiDAR), can provide high resolution environmental data, such as depth maps, which may indicate the proximity of different objects to the LiDAR.
(Source: US Patent & Trademark Office )
The main takeaway from all the points above is the fact that Apple already has a technology which enables car autonomy. Moreover, the company seems to have a strategy of how to combine different technologies in a final solution, which can help Apple monetize its products.
Apple stock remains a buy It is evident that Apple's self-driving auto program may be much more real than it can seem. The high number of test cars on the roads, patents, and partnerships with the biggest automakers like Volkswagen ( OTCPK:VLKAY ) ( OTCPK:VLKAF ) (the news on that came in on May 23) mean the solution can become ready for the mass market in the coming years. However, this is only one of the reasons to stay long AAPL. The corporation has successfully established several other very promising lines of business which generate a significant amount of revenue and help Apple reduce its reliance on the smartphone market.
For instance, services generate more than $9 billion in quarterly revenue, and the segment grew a hefty 31% year-on-year in the latest quarter. Wearables, which include Apple Watch, Beats and EarPods, increased even more - almost 50%, according to the company's management. It can be expected the trend will continue in the near future, as Apple invests a lot of resources not only in new technologies but also in such topics as original content, which will attract even more users to the ecosystem.
Financially, the state of things also is very favorable for investors. Hence, healthy double-digit revenue growth, stable margins, high level of cash, and low debt are the points that make Apple attractive for investment. Moreover, the latest $100 billion buyback program and growing dividends will likely support the stock even if the market conditions change negatively. Therefore, my price target of $197, calculated using a DCF model in the previous article on Apple, remains in place.
